book-algorithms-to-live-by.title: Algorithms to Live By
book-algorithms-to-live-by.description: Brian Christian and Tom Griffiths on applying computer science algorithms to everyday human decisions.

chapterDescriptions.001: The 37% Rule — optimal stopping theory for when to commit in decisions from apartment hunting to dating.
chapterDescriptions.002: Explore/exploit tradeoffs and the multi-armed bandit problem applied to restaurant choices and career paths.
chapterDescriptions.003: Algorithmic efficiency and Big-O notation as a mental model for prioritising what deserves your attention.
chapterDescriptions.004: Caching, memory hierarchies, and why organising your physical and digital space by frequency of use saves time.
chapterDescriptions.005: Scheduling algorithms — earliest due date, shortest processing time, and how to manage deadlines and interruptions.
chapterDescriptions.006: Overfitting, bias-variance tradeoff, and why more data or more complexity can hurt decision quality.
chapterDescriptions.007: Game theory, Nash equilibrium, and competitive dynamics in auctions, negotiations, and social dilemmas.

book-almanack-of-naval-ravikant.title: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant
book-almanack-of-naval-ravikant.description: Naval Ravikant on wealth creation, happiness as a skill, and the philosophy of self-reliance through leverage, judgment, and integrity.

chapterDescriptions.001: Wealth vs. Money vs. Status — distinguishing real wealth creation from zero-sum status games.
chapterDescriptions.002: Specific knowledge — the unique, authentic expertise that cannot be trained but must be built through curiosity and obsession.
chapterDescriptions.003: Permissionless leverage — capital, code, and media as force multipliers that let you create value without anyone's approval.
chapterDescriptions.004: Judgment over effort — why leverage amplifies bad decisions and how to cultivate better judgment through mental models.
chapterDescriptions.005: Happiness as absence of desire — the Buddhist insight that happiness is the default state when you stop craving.
chapterDescriptions.006: Internal vs external locus of control — taking radical responsibility for your emotional state and circumstances.
chapterDescriptions.007: Choice-less awareness — observing thoughts without identification and the practice of mindfulness as a meta-skill.
chapterDescriptions.008: Reading as the ultimate meta-skill — how to build a reading habit, choose books, and synthesise knowledge across fields.
chapterDescriptions.009: Health as the foundational layer — sleep, nutrition, and exercise as non-negotiable prerequisites for wealth and happiness.
chapterDescriptions.010: Radical authenticity — the power of being yourself in business and life as a competitive advantage.

book-atomic-habits.title: Atomic Habits
book-atomic-habits.description: James Clear on how small daily habits compound into remarkable results.

chapterDescriptions.001: The power of tiny gains — how 1% improvements compound into extraordinary results over time.
chapterDescriptions.002: The three layers of behaviour change — identity, process, and outcome; why identity-based habits stick.
chapterDescriptions.003: The four-step habit loop — cue, craving, response, reward as the neurological backbone of every habit.
chapterDescriptions.004: The habit scorecard — becoming aware of your automatic behaviours before trying to change them.
chapterDescriptions.005: The power of context — how environment design makes good habits inevitable and bad habits impossible.
chapterDescriptions.006: The role of dopamine — how anticipation drives action and the strategy of temptation bundling.
chapterDescriptions.007: Social norms and the power of mimicry — joining cultures where your desired behaviour is the normal behaviour.
chapterDescriptions.008: Motion vs. action — the trap of planning without doing and the importance of the habit of showing up.
chapterDescriptions.009: The cardinal rule of behaviour change — making habits immediately satisfying to reinforce repetition.
chapterDescriptions.010: The Goldilocks Rule — working on tasks of just-manageable difficulty to stay in the flow state.
chapterDescriptions.011: Genetics and habit alignment — why your genes don't determine your destiny but do point to your niche.

book-beginning-of-infinity.title: The Beginning of Infinity
book-beginning-of-infinity.description: David Deutsch on the power of good explanations and the unlimited potential of human knowledge.

chapterDescriptions.001: Good explanations — why the defining feature of scientific knowledge is that it is hard to vary while remaining correct.
chapterDescriptions.002: Fallibilism — the recognition that all knowledge is conjectural and that growth comes from criticism, not certainty.
chapterDescriptions.003: The infinite reach of explanation — how abstract knowledge enables unlimited progress beyond direct experience.
chapterDescriptions.004: Knowledge in evolution — how biological evolution creates knowledge without a knower, and what it shares with science.
chapterDescriptions.005: The many-worlds interpretation — Deutsch's argument that quantum theory implies a multiverse that is real and testable.
chapterDescriptions.006: The Enlightenment — the moment when systematic criticism and problem-solving became institutionalised as progress.
chapterDescriptions.007: The human universal — the unique human capacity for creative explanation and why it is both universal and unlimited.
chapterDescriptions.008: The beginning of infinity — why civilisation is at the start, not the end, of its potential for growth and discovery.

book-bhagavad-gita.title: The Bhagavad Gita
book-bhagavad-gita.description: Ancient Indian philosophical text on duty, righteousness, and self-realization through the dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna.

chapterDescriptions.001: The battlefield of life — Arjuna's moral crisis and the setting of the Gita as a metaphor for inner conflict.
chapterDescriptions.002: Karma Yoga — the path of selfless action; doing your duty without attachment to outcomes.
chapterDescriptions.003: The three gunas — sattva, rajas, and tamas as the fundamental qualities that shape all behaviour and thought.
chapterDescriptions.004: The genesis of anger — how unchecked desire leads to anger, clouded judgment, and spiritual downfall.
chapterDescriptions.005: The universal form — Krishna's revelation as Vishvarupa, the cosmic form containing all of existence.
chapterDescriptions.006: Equanimity in achievement — the practical meaning of success as maintaining balance in both gain and loss.
chapterDescriptions.007: Divine nature — the daivi sampat or divine qualities that elevate human character and action.
chapterDescriptions.008: Samatva — skill in action defined as perfect evenness of mind in success and failure.
chapterDescriptions.009: The divine descent — the concept of avatar and the purpose of divine intervention across ages.
chapterDescriptions.010: Remembering at the final moment — the teaching that your last thought is shaped by your lifelong habits.
chapterDescriptions.011: Austerity of the body — the discipline of physical, verbal, and mental austerity for self-purification.

book-cointelligence.title: Co-Intelligence
book-cointelligence.description: Ethan Mollick on how to live and work with AI as a partner rather than a tool.

chapterDescriptions.001: The Mechanical Turk legacy — why AI is not just another technology but a fundamentally new kind of intelligence.
chapterDescriptions.002: The jagged frontier — where AI excels, where it fails, and why the boundaries are constantly shifting.
chapterDescriptions.003: Always be using AI — the first rule of co-intelligence is deep, continuous engagement to understand the technology.
chapterDescriptions.004: The social interface of AI — how AI changes collaboration, team dynamics, and the nature of work relationships.
chapterDescriptions.005: AI as the ultimate muse — using generative AI for creativity, ideation, and breaking creative blocks.
chapterDescriptions.006: The coworker paradigm — treating AI as a collaborator rather than a tool for delegation or automation.
chapterDescriptions.007: The homework apocalypse — how AI disrupts education and assessment, and what meaningful learning looks like next.
chapterDescriptions.008: AI as the personal coach — leveraging AI for personalised learning, skill development, and reflective practice.
chapterDescriptions.009: The future of co-intelligence — emerging capabilities and the long-term trajectory of human-AI partnership.
chapterDescriptions.010: The great disruption — societal implications, inequality risks, and the choices that will shape our AI future.

book-deep-work.title: Deep Work
book-deep-work.description: Cal Newport on the value of focused, distraction-free concentration in a distracted world.

chapterDescriptions.001: Deep work defined — professional activities performed in a state of distraction-free concentration that push cognitive capabilities.
chapterDescriptions.002: The neurological argument for depth — how deep work rewires the brain for attention, meaning, and satisfaction.
chapterDescriptions.003: The monastic philosophy — eliminating shallow obligations entirely to maximise depth, and who this suits.
chapterDescriptions.004: Don't take breaks from distraction — training attention by scheduling distraction instead of scheduling focus.
chapterDescriptions.005: The craftsman approach to tool selection — choosing digital tools based on their impact on deep work, not their novelty.
chapterDescriptions.006: Schedule every minute of your day — the time-blocking method for making deep work a non-negotiable part of your routine.
chapterDescriptions.007: The deep work equation — turning deep work into a measurable, repeatable practice through metrics and ritual.

book-get-better-at-anything.title: Get Better at Anything
book-get-better-at-anything.description: Scott H. Young on the science of learning and how to master any skill.

chapterDescriptions.001: Problem solving is search — why learning something new is like navigating an unfamiliar space, and how to explore efficiently.
chapterDescriptions.002: Success is the best teacher — the role of prior knowledge and why you learn faster by building on what you already know.
chapterDescriptions.003: Difficulty has a sweet spot — the Goldilocks zone of challenge where learning accelerates most rapidly.
chapterDescriptions.004: Variability over repetition — why varied practice builds transferable skills better than rote repetition.
chapterDescriptions.005: Experience does not reliably ensure expertise — the difference between mere time spent and deliberate practice.
chapterDescriptions.006: Practice must meet reality — why learning in context and testing yourself under realistic conditions matters.
chapterDescriptions.007: Fears fade with exposure — the psychology of anxiety in learning and how graded exposure builds confidence.
chapterDescriptions.008: Learning through multiple principles — synthesising different strategies to accelerate mastery across domains.

book-influence.title: Influence
book-influence.description: Robert Cialdini on the psychology of persuasion and the six principles of influence.

chapterDescriptions.001: Reciprocity — the rule that we feel obligated to return favours, and how savvy persuaders use it to gain compliance.
chapterDescriptions.002: Commitment and consistency — once we take a stand, we tend to behave in ways consistent with that commitment.
chapterDescriptions.003: Social proof — the tendency to see an action as correct when others are doing it, especially in uncertainty.
chapterDescriptions.004: Authority — the deep-seated sense of duty to authority figures and the dangers of blind obedience.
chapterDescriptions.005: Liking — people prefer to say yes to those they like; physical attractiveness, similarity, and compliments drive this.
chapterDescriptions.006: Scarcity — opportunities seem more valuable when they are less available; the limited-number and deadline tactics.
chapterDescriptions.007: Integrated influence tactics — how professional compliance professionals combine multiple principles for maximum effect.
chapterDescriptions.008: Identifying the core principle — recognising which influence principle is being used in real-world persuasion attempts.

book-seeking-wisdom-darwin-to-munger.title: Seeking Wisdom: From Darwin to Munger
book-seeking-wisdom-darwin-to-munger.description: Peter Bevelin on mental models and decision-making drawn from biology, psychology, and philosophy.

chapterDescriptions.001: Anatomy shapes behaviour — how biological structure and evolution constrain and direct human decision-making.
chapterDescriptions.002: Confirmation bias — the tendency to seek evidence that confirms existing beliefs and how to counteract it.
chapterDescriptions.003: Understanding scale and probability — how misjudging scale, risk, and probability leads to systematic errors.
chapterDescriptions.004: Systems thinking — seeing the interconnectedness of variables and avoiding narrow, linear cause-effect reasoning.
chapterDescriptions.005: Latticework of mental models — building an interconnected network of models from multiple disciplines for better reasoning.
chapterDescriptions.006: Opportunity cost — recognising that every choice excludes alternatives and that tradeoffs are universal.
chapterDescriptions.007: Lollapalooza effect — the confluence of multiple biases and tendencies that produces extreme, non-linear outcomes.
chapterDescriptions.008: Munger prescriptions for misery — inversion as a practical tool: studying failure to learn what to avoid.

book-super-thinking.title: Super Thinking
book-super-thinking.description: Gabriel Weinberg and Lauren McCann on mental models for better reasoning and decision-making.

chapterDescriptions.001: Occam's Razor and the simplest explanation — why parsimony is a useful heuristic and when it fails.
chapterDescriptions.002: Confirmation bias and motivated reasoning — how our desires distort perception and how to build debiasing habits.
chapterDescriptions.003: Circle of competence — knowing the boundaries of your knowledge and why operating outside them is dangerous.
chapterDescriptions.004: Thermodynamics and entropy — physical laws as mental models for understanding energy, order, and decay in systems.
chapterDescriptions.005: Natural selection and adaptation — evolutionary thinking applied to competition, innovation, and organisational change.
chapterDescriptions.006: Microeconomics and incentives — supply, demand, and the power of incentives in shaping behaviour at scale.
chapterDescriptions.007: Climate change through mental models — applying multiple frameworks to understand a complex, systemic challenge.
chapterDescriptions.008: Complexity bias vs Occam's Razor — when simple explanations mislead and the world truly requires nuanced models.
chapterDescriptions.009: Parkinson's Law — work expands to fill the time available; how constraints improve productivity and focus.
chapterDescriptions.010: Game theory and strategic interaction — Nash equilibrium, prisoner's dilemma, and co-operation in competitive settings.
chapterDescriptions.011: Deliberate practice and the learning curve — the mental models behind skill acquisition and mastery.

book-the-adaptive-edge.title: The Adaptive Edge
book-the-adaptive-edge.description: Leadership frameworks for navigating complexity and driving organizational change.

chapterDescriptions.001: The illusion of the broken system — reframing organisational problems as adaptive challenges rather than technical failures.
chapterDescriptions.002: The view from above — developing the balcony perspective to see patterns and dynamics beyond the dance floor.
chapterDescriptions.003: The goal of diagnosis — distinguishing technical problems from adaptive challenges before prescribing solutions.
chapterDescriptions.004: Diagnosing the self — turning the diagnostic lens inward to examine your own assumptions and leadership biases.
chapterDescriptions.005: The nature of interventions — why small, well-timed interventions can create outsized impact in complex systems.
chapterDescriptions.006: The danger of leading — the risks leaders take when they challenge the status quo and how to manage exposure.
chapterDescriptions.007: Thriving through change — building resilience and adaptive capacity in yourself and your organisation.
chapterDescriptions.008: The myth of the fix-it leader — letting go of the saviour mindset and empowering distributed problem-solving.
chapterDescriptions.009: The discipline of self-correction — creating feedback loops that allow you to course-correct before failure.
chapterDescriptions.010: The essence of adaptive leadership — mobilising people to tackle tough challenges and thrive in uncertainty.
chapterDescriptions.011: The nature of adaptive challenges — why adaptive problems require changes in values, beliefs, and behaviours.
chapterDescriptions.012: The danger of misinterpretation — how misdiagnosing adaptive challenges as technical problems leads to failure.
chapterDescriptions.013: The integration of adaptive leadership — weaving adaptive principles into daily leadership practice.
chapterDescriptions.014: Technical vs adaptive misdiagnosis — deeper exploration of the most common and costly leadership error.
chapterDescriptions.015: Leading beyond boundaries — applying adaptive leadership across organisational and cultural boundaries.
chapterDescriptions.016: The daily balcony — the discipline of stepping back regularly to reflect, reframe, and recalibrate your leadership.

book-the-changing-world-order.title: The Changing World Order
book-the-changing-world-order.description: Ray Dalio on the repeating cycles of empires, economies, and the big cycle of history.

chapterDescriptions.001: The Big Cycle — how empires rise and fall in predictable patterns over decades and centuries.
chapterDescriptions.002: The determinants of power — the eight key metrics that measure a nation's strength and trajectory.
chapterDescriptions.003: The long-term debt cycle — how debt accumulation and deleveraging drive the rise and fall of empires.
chapterDescriptions.004: The six stages of internal order — the predictable phases from new order to revolution within a nation.
chapterDescriptions.005: The external order and the Thucydides Trap — what happens when a rising power challenges an established one.
chapterDescriptions.006: The rise and fall of the Dutch Empire — the first modern empire's ascent and decline as a case study in the big cycle.
chapterDescriptions.007: The future of the US and China — applying the framework to forecast the next phase of the great power competition.
chapterDescriptions.008: The last 500 years in a nutshell — a condensed tour of the big cycle across Dutch, British, American, and Chinese history.
chapterDescriptions.009: The Dutch Golden Age and education — how universal literacy and printing fuelled the Dutch economic miracle.
chapterDescriptions.010: The British rise and the Industrial Revolution — the confluence of finance, coal, and navigation that built the British Empire.
chapterDescriptions.011: The 1945 new world order — the post-war settlement that established American dominance and the global institutions we know today.
chapterDescriptions.012: The long history of Chinese cycles — how China's dynastic cycles map onto the big cycle framework across millennia.
chapterDescriptions.013: The three determinants of the future — wealth, power, and the internal order as the pillars shaping what comes next.
chapterDescriptions.014: The wealth gap and the internal cycle — how inequality drives the internal cycle of populism, conflict, and revolution.
chapterDescriptions.015: The Mandate of Heaven and cyclical history — the ancient Chinese concept of dynastic legitimacy and its resonance with modern cycles.

book-the-great-mental-models-v1.title: The Great Mental Models Volume 1
book-the-great-mental-models-v1.description: Shane Parrish and Rhiannon Beaubien on the fundamental mental models from physics, biology, and systems thinking that improve decision-making.

chapterDescriptions.001: Mental model definition — what mental models are and why building a latticework of them improves decision-making.
chapterDescriptions.002: Map as abstraction — recognising that every map (model) is a simplification and that the territory is always more complex.
chapterDescriptions.003: Circle of competence — knowing the boundaries of your expertise and operating only where you have genuine insight.
chapterDescriptions.004: First principles reasoning — breaking problems down to their fundamental truths and rebuilding from there.
chapterDescriptions.005: First vs second-order thinking — anticipating the knock-on effects of decisions beyond the immediate consequences.
chapterDescriptions.006: Probabilistic thinking — embracing uncertainty by thinking in probabilities rather than certainties.
chapterDescriptions.007: Inversion — approaching problems backwards by asking what you want to avoid or what could cause failure.
chapterDescriptions.008: Occam's Razor — the principle that simpler explanations are generally more likely to be correct.
chapterDescriptions.009: Hanlon's Razor — not attributing to malice what can be adequately explained by ignorance or incompetence.
chapterDescriptions.010: The Pareto Principle — the 80/20 rule that a minority of inputs produce the majority of outcomes.
chapterDescriptions.011: Latticework of mental models — the value of having a diverse toolkit of models from multiple disciplines.

book-the-great-mental-models-v2.title: The Great Mental Models Volume 2
book-the-great-mental-models-v2.description: Shane Parrish and Rhiannon Beaubien on mental models from chemistry, mathematics, and systems thinking for better decision-making.

chapterDescriptions.001: Relativity and frames of reference — how your perspective shapes reality and the power of shifting your reference point.
chapterDescriptions.002: Inertia — the tendency of systems and people to resist change unless sufficient force is applied.
chapterDescriptions.003: Friction — the hidden forces that slow progress and how identifying them reveals the path to improvement.
chapterDescriptions.004: Leverage — using small forces at the right point to create disproportionate impact across systems.
chapterDescriptions.005: Speed vs velocity — the difference between mere activity (speed) and purposeful progress toward a goal (velocity).
chapterDescriptions.006: Conservation of energy — the principle that energy is never lost, only transformed, as a lens for understanding tradeoffs.
chapterDescriptions.007: Activation energy — the initial hurdle that must be overcome before a reaction or habit takes hold.
chapterDescriptions.008: Catalysts — agents that accelerate change without being consumed, and how they apply to organisations and relationships.
chapterDescriptions.009: Alloys — how combining elements creates materials stronger than any individual component, applied to teams and ideas.
chapterDescriptions.010: Concentration — the power of focus and the insight that depth beats breadth for achieving mastery and results.
chapterDescriptions.011: Ecosystems and interconnectedness — understanding that everything is connected and that isolated interventions have ripple effects.
chapterDescriptions.012: Keystone species — the critical entities whose presence disproportionately shapes and stabilises entire systems.
chapterDescriptions.013: Natural selection — the engine of evolution as a mental model for competition, adaptation, and survival.
chapterDescriptions.014: The Red Queen Effect — the need to keep running just to stay in place when competitors are also improving.
chapterDescriptions.015: Competitive exclusion — the principle that two competitors cannot occupy the same niche indefinitely.

book-the-great-mental-models-v3.title: The Great Mental Models Volume 3
book-the-great-mental-models-v3.description: Shane Parrish and Rhiannon Beaubien on mental models from systems thinking and mathematics for better decision-making.

chapterDescriptions.001: Reinforcing feedback loops — how small changes can amplify themselves, driving growth or collapse in systems.
chapterDescriptions.002: Homeostasis — the tendency of systems to self-regulate and resist change, and how to work with or around it.
chapterDescriptions.003: The theory of constraints — identifying the single bottleneck that limits a system's throughput and focusing there.
chapterDescriptions.004: Margin of safety — building buffers and redundancy to protect against uncertainty and worst-case scenarios.
chapterDescriptions.005: Churn — the rate at which participants leave a system, and why reducing churn is often more effective than acquiring new ones.
chapterDescriptions.006: Irreducibility — recognising phenomena that cannot be simplified without losing their essential nature.
chapterDescriptions.007: Compounding — the exponential growth that results when gains accumulate on previous gains across any domain.
chapterDescriptions.008: The law of diminishing returns — the point at which additional input yields progressively smaller output.
chapterDescriptions.009: Regression to the mean — why extreme outcomes tend to be followed by more average ones, and the trap of misattribution.
chapterDescriptions.010: Sampling — how representative samples reveal population truths and the dangers of biased or small samples.
chapterDescriptions.011: The normal distribution — understanding bell curves, standard deviations, and where most outcomes cluster.
chapterDescriptions.012: Algorithms — step-by-step procedures that guarantee correct outcomes, and when to use them versus heuristics.
chapterDescriptions.013: Permutations — counting arrangements and possibilities as a foundation for understanding probability and risk.
chapterDescriptions.014: Expected value — weighing outcomes by their probability to make rational decisions under uncertainty.
chapterDescriptions.015: Correlation vs causation — the classic statistical trap of mistaking relationships for causes.
chapterDescriptions.016: Critical mass — the threshold beyond which a system undergoes a self-sustaining transformation.
chapterDescriptions.017: Structure determines behaviour — the systems thinking insight that patterns of behaviour are built into system design.

book-the-great-mental-models-v4.title: The Great Mental Models Volume 4
book-the-great-mental-models-v4.description: Shane Parrish and Rhiannon Beaubien on mental models from economics and art for better decision-making.

chapterDescriptions.001: Scarcity — the fundamental economic problem of unlimited wants versus limited resources and its psychological effects.
chapterDescriptions.002: Specialisation and division of labour — how focused expertise drives productivity gains and economic complexity.
chapterDescriptions.003: Pure monopoly pricing power — what happens when a single seller controls a market and how monopolies set prices.
chapterDescriptions.004: Audience awareness — the artist's skill of anticipating how an audience will perceive and interpret a work.
chapterDescriptions.005: Representation vs reality — the gap between how things are presented and how they truly are, across art and life.
chapterDescriptions.006: Contextual architecture — how the physical and social environment shapes behaviour and meaning.

book-the-psychology-of-money.title: The Psychology of Money
book-the-psychology-of-money.description: Morgan Housel on the emotional and behavioral side of financial decision-making.

chapterDescriptions.001: The lens of experience — why your personal financial history shapes your money decisions more than any textbook.
chapterDescriptions.002: The invisible siblings — the role of luck and risk in financial outcomes and why we ignore outcomes that didn't happen.
chapterDescriptions.003: The moving goalpost — the hedonic treadmill that makes enough never feel like enough after you reach it.
chapterDescriptions.004: The unintuitive nature of math — why compounding returns are hard to grasp and why our intuition about growth is wrong.
chapterDescriptions.005: The dual skillset — the separation of knowing what to do (financial intelligence) from doing it (behavioural discipline).
chapterDescriptions.006: Tail events — the few extreme events that drive the majority of outcomes across investing, business, and life.
chapterDescriptions.007: The highest form of wealth — the freedom to do what you want, when you want, with whom you want.
chapterDescriptions.008: The paradox of admiration — why we respect wealth in others but rarely consider what they sacrificed to get it.
chapterDescriptions.009: Wealth is what you don't see — the difference between visible spending (income) and invisible assets (wealth).
chapterDescriptions.010: The efficiency of saving — how the single most controllable variable in financial success is your savings rate.
chapterDescriptions.011: Rational vs reasonable — why being mathematically rational with money is less important than being psychologically reasonable.
chapterDescriptions.012: The problem with history as a map — why past financial data is an imperfect guide to future outcomes.
chapterDescriptions.013: The margin of safety — the power of having enough room for error to survive when things go wrong.
chapterDescriptions.014: The end of history illusion — the tendency to underestimate how much our future selves will change from who we are now.
chapterDescriptions.015: The hidden price tag — the real costs of investing: volatility, uncertainty, and the emotional toll of being wrong.
chapterDescriptions.016: The game selection — choosing the financial game that suits your personality rather than chasing everyone else's.
chapterDescriptions.017: The popularity of pessimism — why bad news sells and why pessimism sounds smarter than optimism in finance.
chapterDescriptions.018: The power of narrative — how compelling stories drive economic and market behaviour more than cold numbers.
chapterDescriptions.019: The goal of financial decisions — defining what money is actually for: control over your time and life.
chapterDescriptions.020: The post-war reset — how the post-war generation's experience of scarcity shaped a uniquely cautious financial psychology.

book-the-startup-of-you.title: The Startup of You
book-the-startup-of-you.description: Reid Hoffman and Ben Casnocha on applying startup principles to career building.

chapterDescriptions.001: Permanent beta — treating your career as a product that is never finished, always iterating and improving.
chapterDescriptions.002: The three pieces of the puzzle — your assets, aspirations, and market realities as the framework for career strategy.
chapterDescriptions.003: ABZ planning — having an A plan (current path), B plan (pivot), and Z plan (safety net) for career resilience.
chapterDescriptions.004: The 'I' is 'We' — why your professional network is your most valuable asset and how to invest in it systematically.
chapterDescriptions.005: Breakout opportunities — recognising the rare moments that combine high potential with a unique fit for your skills.
chapterDescriptions.006: Redefining risk — why the most risky career move is often playing it safe in a rapidly changing economy.
chapterDescriptions.007: Network intelligence — the ability to tap into your network for information, introductions, and serendipitous opportunities.
chapterDescriptions.008: The entrepreneurship of life — applying startup principles to every domain from career to health to relationships.
chapterDescriptions.009: The intersection of the three pieces — finding the sweet spot where your assets, aspirations, and market realities converge.

coursera-financial-markets-global.title: Financial Markets
coursera-financial-markets-global.description: Robert Shiller's Yale course on financial markets, risk management, and behavioral finance.

chapterDescriptions.001: The law of large numbers — how insurance works by pooling risk across many independent events.
chapterDescriptions.002: The concept of equity and ownership — what it means to own a share of a company and the rights that come with it.
chapterDescriptions.003: Loss aversion — the psychological finding that losses hurt roughly twice as much as equivalent gains feel good.
chapterDescriptions.004: The mechanics of a bond — how fixed-income securities work, from coupons to yield to maturity.
chapterDescriptions.005: The nature of a mortgage — the structure of real estate debt and how securitisation transforms it into traded assets.
chapterDescriptions.006: Fractional reserve banking — how banks create money by lending more than they hold in reserves.
chapterDescriptions.007: The definition of a derivative — a financial contract whose value derives from an underlying asset or benchmark.
chapterDescriptions.008: The social purpose of finance — the role of financial markets in allocating capital to productive uses across the economy.
chapterDescriptions.009: The mechanics of exchange rates — how currency values are determined by supply, demand, and central bank policy.
chapterDescriptions.010: The rise of robo-advisors — how algorithms are democratising investment advice and portfolio management.
chapterDescriptions.011: The nature of a financial crisis — the anatomy of systemic collapse from asset bubbles to contagion.
chapterDescriptions.012: Systematic vs unsystematic risk — the distinction between market-wide risk that cannot be diversified away and asset-specific risk.

coursera-finding-purpose-and-meaning-in-.title: Finding Purpose and Meaning in Life
coursera-finding-purpose-and-meaning-in-.description: Advanced masterclass on the philosophy, science, and practice of discovering and living a life of purpose.

chapterDescriptions.001: Socrates' challenge — the examined life as the foundation of meaning and the question of what makes life worth living.
chapterDescriptions.002: The Ryff well-being framework — the six dimensions of psychological well-being from autonomy to personal growth.
chapterDescriptions.003: Value internalisation — the difference between goals that are truly yours and goals adopted from others' expectations.
chapterDescriptions.004: Post-traumatic growth — the discovery that adversity can be a catalyst for deepened meaning and personal transformation.
chapterDescriptions.005: The four circles — mapping your life into relationships, work, self, and spirituality to find balance and purpose.
chapterDescriptions.006: Job crafting — reshaping your work role to better align with your strengths, values, and sense of meaning.

coursera-genai-for-algorithmic-trading.title: Generative AI for Algorithmic Trading
coursera-genai-for-algorithmic-trading.description: Integrating large language models and generative AI into quantitative trading strategies.

chapterDescriptions.001: Integrating LLMs with quantitative strategies — the architecture of combining large language models with traditional quant methods.
chapterDescriptions.002: Sentiment extraction from financial news — how NLP pipelines turn unstructured news text into tradeable sentiment signals.
chapterDescriptions.003: Pattern recognition with GenAI — using generative models to identify market patterns that traditional quant models miss.
chapterDescriptions.004: Understanding LSTM memory in trading — how long short-term memory networks capture temporal dependencies in price data.
chapterDescriptions.005: The goal of explainable AI in finance — why black-box models are problematic for regulated financial decisions.
chapterDescriptions.006: The role of sentiment scores in quantitative models — combining fundamental data with sentiment for richer trading signals.
chapterDescriptions.007: Handling live streaming data — the architecture for processing real-time market data with AI models.
chapterDescriptions.008: The architecture of a GenAI trading pipeline — end-to-end design from data ingestion to order execution.
chapterDescriptions.009: AI-driven efficient frontier — using generative models to optimise portfolio allocation along the risk-return curve.
chapterDescriptions.010: Detecting tail risk via linguistic cues — how language patterns in news and reports can predict rare market events.
chapterDescriptions.011: The anatomy of an autonomous trading agent — the components of a self-contained AI system that makes and executes trades.

podcast-age-of-async-agents.title: The Age of Async Agents
podcast-age-of-async-agents.description: Swyx hosts Walden Yan (Cognition/Devin) and Cole Murray (OpenInspect) on the three waves of AI coding tools and async agent architectures.

chapterDescriptions.001: Three waves of AI coding tools — from copilots to agents to autonomous systems, tracing the evolution of AI-assisted development.
chapterDescriptions.002: Devin's commit percentage growth — how AI coding agents improve over time and what the learning curve looks like.
chapterDescriptions.003: Harness in the box — the architecture of sandboxed execution environments for safe agent deployment.
chapterDescriptions.004: Docker limitations for agents — why container-based isolation falls short for long-running, stateful agent workloads.
